correctness.rationale: For every finite abelian H and every m≥2, horizontal character orthogonality forces one singleton and n−1 doubleton vertical-frequency fibers. Removal of a single spatial row from the complete-strip matrix makes a codimension-one orthogonal projection of squared norm 1/(2n), hence exact determinant. An exact Sherman–Morrison calculation gives v*Q⁻¹v=2n−1, the Rayleigh obstruction λmin≤1, and a trace inequality λmax≥2n; equality forces every doubleton antipodal. The odd-m secular polynomial is independently reconstructed from its three eigenlevels and projection weights, with exact symbolic expansion and an all-parameter analytic proof. The packaged verifier directly reconstructs full Fourier matrices for cyclic and noncyclic H, with exhaustive small-case partner counts; finite computations are not used as proof of universal quantifiers. A special n=2 case and vertical m=2 are included without claiming novelty of known elementary boundaries.

originality.rationale: The natural published starting point arXiv:1904.04487 has quantitative Riesz definitions, a subgroup-plus-one-point case, an intact two-layer product, and a relocated point, but neither its full statements nor its product theorem cover deleting exactly one sample from a two-layer product while optimizing all Fourier basis partners. Two most similar complete mathematical records were read: the subgroup-plus-point case has n+1 rather than 2n−1 sites and the opposite fiber occupancy, while the intersecting-two-line case has 2p sites and uses unicyclic incidence geometry, not parallel horizontal fibers. Even though the subgroup-plus-point case shares an even-order 2n ratio, that equality alone does not imply the new universal punctured-product theorem. Current full-text and database searches do not establish priority beyond these comparisons; prior elementary co-singleton m=2 and smallest n=2 subcases are acknowledged.
residual_risks: A historic principal-minor or deleted-row Fourier lemma might imply boundary cases, particularly m=2.
An unindexed exact all-partner result under punctured Cartesian character tables/Schur complements could imply part of the statement.
The full odd-order condition-number optimum is not claimed or known from the analysis.

value.rationale: A single spatial erasure turns a uniformly well-conditioned two-layer Fourier sampling product into a set whose EVERY unweighted exponential basis has squared condition number at least 2n; this is a quantitative structural instability growing arbitrarily with horizontal group order. The theorem additionally optimizes determinant and classifies every optimizer for all vertical orders and every finite abelian H, and for even orders exactly determines the best lower/upper bounds and conditioning with all equality cases. The odd-order determinant-optimal secular spectrum gives extra constructive design information. These solve natural finite harmonic sampling robustness questions rather than arbitrary fixed-table computations or routine normalization checks.
